content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "When faced with differing opinions, we should try to reach agreement through friendly discussion and reasonable argument." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
content.topic: Reaching agreement through friendly discussion and reasonable argument

modelEssay.title: Reaching Agreement Through Friendly Discussion
modelEssay.content:
When faced with differing opinions, we should try to reach agreement through friendly discussion and reasonable argument. Disagreement is inevitable wherever people think independently, but the way we handle it determines whether it divides us or brings us closer.

A friendly attitude keeps the door of communication open. Once a conversation turns into a quarrel, both sides stop listening and start defending themselves, and even the soundest idea will be rejected simply because of who proposed it. By contrast, when we speak with respect and genuine curiosity, the other party is far more willing to reconsider his or her position. Reasonable argument matters just as much: evidence, logic and concrete examples persuade people, while raising one's voice never does.

I experienced this in a group project last term. My teammates and I disagreed sharply over the research topic, yet instead of insisting on our own preferences, we listed the pros and cons of each proposal and finally settled on a plan better than any single one of them.

In short, patience and reason are the shortest path from disagreement to consensus.

structureAnalysis.paragraph1: 开篇段：照抄题目给定首句并给出总观点——分歧不可避免，处理方式决定结果
structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 论证段：从'友好态度'与'理性论证'两个角度说明为何这种方式有效，用对比手法凸显争吵的害处
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 例证段：以小组作业中的实际经历佐证观点，落到具体做法（罗列利弊、达成更优方案）
structureAnalysis.paragraph4: 结论段：一句话收束，重申耐心与理性是化解分歧的最短路径

highlights: 首句严格照抄题目要求的句子，符合 CET6 给定首句作文的评分要求
使用 keeps the door of communication open、the shortest path from disagreement to consensus 等形象表达
运用 Once...、By contrast...、just as much 等衔接手段，论证层次清晰
个人经历段落具体到'列出利弊、最终方案优于任一单独提案'，避免空泛举例

transcript.text: Have you decided what you wish to study?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你想好要学什么了吗？

transcript.text: Yes, Professor.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 想好了，教授。

transcript.text: I wish to study architecture.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我想学建筑学。

transcript.text: Ah, that's a wonderful profession.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 啊，那是个很棒的职业。

transcript.text: Why did you choose it?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你为什么选择它？

transcript.text: I gave a lot of thought to things you said during our last discussion, and I decided architecture made the most sense for me.

transcript.translation: 我认真思考了上次讨论时您说的那些话，最后认定建筑学对我来说最合适。

transcript.text: In particular, I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 尤其是，我被设计与工程的结合所吸引。

transcript.text: That's great, but I seem to remember you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 很好，不过我记得你之前一直担心那些高深的数学。

transcript.text: You no longer think this aspect will be too hard for you?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你现在不觉得这方面对你来说太难了吗？

transcript.text: No, I was doing some online research, and I think I should be able to manage.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 不觉得了，我在网上查了些资料，我想我应该能应付得来。

transcript.text: Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I'll simply put in the work required.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 数学可能是课程中我会遇到的最难的科目，但我就是肯下所需要的功夫。

transcript.text: I'm certain the fruits of my labour will pay off.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我相信我的付出会有回报。

transcript.text: I'm sure that's true.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我相信确实如此。

transcript.text: Due to its material nature, architecture is one field where you'll be able to clearly witness the contribution you make to a city, and the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 由于建筑具有实体性，在这个领域里你能清楚地看到自己对一座城市的贡献，而你所留下的作品会比我们这些凡人存在得久远得多。

transcript.text: Yeah, I guess that's true too.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是啊，我想这话也没错。

transcript.text: So what subjects do you think I should start brushing up on in preparation?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那您觉得我该先温习哪些科目来做准备呢？

transcript.text: I have the whole summer.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我有一整个暑假。

transcript.text: These days, architecture is a very diverse and dynamic degree.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 如今建筑学是一个非常多元、非常有活力的专业。

transcript.text: Most universities will encourage you to learn different things from fields as wide-ranging as philosophy and economics.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 大多数大学都会鼓励你去学习哲学、经济学等各种不同领域的知识。

transcript.text: Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science, because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不过，我建议你从计算机科学入手，因为你在做项目时需要制作大量复杂的视觉图形。

transcript.text: Any software in particular you think I should start with?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 您觉得我应该先从哪个软件学起？

transcript.text: Photoshop is a good place.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: Photoshop 是个不错的起点。

transcript.text: If you aren't yet, try to become as proficient as you can with it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 如果你还不熟练，就尽量把它练到精通。

transcript.text: And another thing that I would recommend you learn as much as you can is fine arts.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 另外我还建议你尽可能多学一些美术方面的知识。

transcript.text: In particular, the history of Western art.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 尤其是西方艺术史。

transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 短文一。

transcript.text: Sports like rock climbing, surfing, skiing and mountain biking thus have lots of appeal.
transcript.translation: 因此，攀岩、冲浪、滑雪和山地自行车这类运动很有吸引力。

transcript.text: They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity.
transcript.translation: 它们没有传统团队运动那么多的规则和压力，却同样具备户外体育活动的全部益处。

transcript.text: When properly supervised, extreme sports can be a part of a healthy, balanced life.
transcript.translation: 在得到恰当监督的情况下，极限运动可以成为健康、均衡生活的一部分。

transcript.text: Some adventure sports may be associated with high risks of injury, so it's important for kids to figure out when to take risks and when not to.
transcript.translation: 有些冒险运动可能伴随较高的受伤风险，因此孩子们弄清楚何时该冒险、何时不该冒险很重要。

transcript.text: Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears.
transcript.translation: 毫无风险的活动会剥夺孩子考验自己、克服恐惧的机会。

transcript.text: But to some, these very risks are what makes these sports a bad choice.
transcript.translation: 但在一些人看来，正是这些风险使这类运动成为糟糕的选择。

transcript.text: They say that extreme sports can often lead to devastating injuries, especially as young thrill seekers may attempt feats that are too advanced for them.
transcript.translation: 他们说极限运动常常会导致严重的伤害，尤其是年轻的刺激追求者可能会尝试超出自己能力的高难度动作。

transcript.text: But let's be real.
transcript.translation: 但我们现实一点。

transcript.text: Most kids do all kinds of dangerous stuff whether you want them to or not.
transcript.translation: 不管你愿不愿意，大多数孩子都会去做各种危险的事。

transcript.text: Adventure sports have many of the same risks and dangers, but they have an additional sense of adventure, courage and autonomy that is important to foster in young children.
transcript.translation: 冒险运动有许多同样的风险和危险，但它们还额外带来冒险精神、勇气和自主性，而这些正是幼儿身上需要培养的。

transcript.text: As always, it's up to parents to decide what's best for their kids.
transcript.translation: 一如既往，什么对孩子最好要由家长来决定。

transcript.text: But if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives.
transcript.translation: 但如果你确实认为冒险运动有点过头了，那就务必尝试把其他形式的户外冒险引入他们的生活。

transcript.text: Camping under the stars, fishing, stargazing or even just playing in the woods can help a lot in building the same sense of self-confidence and risk-taking as in adventure sports.
transcript.translation: 露天野营、钓鱼、观星，甚至只是在树林里玩耍，都能极大地帮助孩子建立起与冒险运动同样的自信心和冒险意识。

questions.questionText: Why do extreme sports appeal to many kids?

options.label: A
options.text: They bring more benefits to young people.

options.label: B
options.text: They require less supervision and training.

options.label: C
options.text: They are more suitable to young people.

options.label: D
options.text: They have fewer rules and pressures.

questions.analysis: 短文开头指出攀岩、冲浪、滑雪、山地自行车等运动很有吸引力，原因是「They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity」，即规则和压力少，故选 D。A 把「同样具有户外运动的益处」偷换成「益处更多」。

questions.questionText: What does the speaker say about risk-free activities?

options.label: A
options.text: They prevent kids from enjoying adventure sports.

options.label: B
options.text: They help kids guard against any possible injuries.

options.label: C
options.text: They rob kids of the chance to cultivate their courage.

options.label: D
options.text: They deprive kids of the opportunity to develop team spirit.

questions.analysis: 原文「Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears」，即无风险活动剥夺了孩子考验自己、克服恐惧的机会，克服恐惧即培养勇气，故选 C。D 把 overcome their fears 偷换成 develop team spirit。

questions.questionText: What should parents do if they decide adventure sports are a bit too much for their kids?

options.label: A
options.text: Help them take up these sports when they are more mature.

options.label: B
options.text: Let them participate in some less risky outdoor activities.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask them to try some forms of indoor sports.

options.label: D
options.text: Introduce them to these sports step by step.

questions.analysis: 结尾建议「if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives」，并举例露营、钓鱼、观星、在树林里玩，都是风险较低的户外活动，故选 B。C 的 indoor（室内）与原文 outdoor 相反；D 是「循序渐进地引导他们做这些极限运动」，与「改做别的活动」不同。

transcript.translation: 短文二。

transcript.text: The shiny gadgets of today will be waste tomorrow.
transcript.translation: 今天光鲜亮丽的电子产品，明天就会变成垃圾。

transcript.text: Manufacturers don't talk much about this when they announce the big new thing that will replace your mostly just as good old thing.
transcript.translation: 厂商在发布那些用来取代你手中其实同样好用的旧产品的新品时，对此几乎只字不提。

transcript.text: In fact, technology firms often purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired, so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one.
transcript.translation: 事实上，科技公司常常故意把设备设计成寿命不长且无法维修，这样消费者就不得不掏钱买新的。

transcript.text: This year, the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score.
transcript.translation: 今年，法国政府开始要求科技厂商标注可维修性评分。

transcript.text: If a device can be repaired, then its life can be extended, saving consumers money and the planet the burden of so many trashed gadgets.
transcript.translation: 如果一台设备可以维修，它的寿命就能延长，既为消费者省钱，也让地球免于承受如此多废弃电子产品的负担。

transcript.text: Equipped with this knowledge, consumers can make better choices about which products to buy.
transcript.translation: 掌握了这些信息，消费者就能更好地选择该买哪些产品。

transcript.text: Some 59 million tons of old TVs, computers, screens, smartphones, washers and other electronics are discarded every year.
transcript.translation: 每年约有 5900 万吨废旧电视、电脑、显示屏、智能手机、洗衣机等电子产品被丢弃。

transcript.text: This waste is dangerous.
transcript.translation: 这些垃圾很危险。

transcript.text: Batteries explode in recycling facilities.
transcript.translation: 电池会在回收设施中爆炸。

transcript.text: Toxic substances like mercury leak into soil and groundwater and disperse in the air.
transcript.translation: 汞等有毒物质会渗入土壤和地下水，并扩散到空气中。

transcript.text: Manufacturing flat screens adds greenhouse gases to the atmosphere.
transcript.translation: 制造平板显示屏会向大气中排放温室气体。

transcript.text: We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem.
transcript.translation: 我们需要科技公司带头解决这个问题。

transcript.text: If they won't, governments must make them do so.
transcript.translation: 如果它们不愿意，政府就必须迫使它们这样做。

transcript.text: Although tech companies will often speak of environmental sustainability, many lobby against repair legislation, fearful it will eat into their profits.
transcript.translation: 尽管科技公司常把环境可持续性挂在嘴边，许多公司却在游说反对维修立法，担心这会侵蚀它们的利润。

transcript.text: Sustainability matters, but marketable design appears to matter more to these companies.
transcript.translation: 可持续性固然重要，但对这些公司来说，好卖的设计似乎更重要。

transcript.text: Consumers should support right to repair legislation.
transcript.translation: 消费者应当支持维修权立法。

transcript.text: In this world, damage is a certainty, but we cannot leave things broken.
transcript.translation: 在这个世界上，损坏是必然的，但我们不能任由东西一直坏着。

transcript.text: A problem of our creation is a problem that can be fixed.
transcript.translation: 我们自己造成的问题，是可以解决的问题。

transcript.text: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
transcript.translation: 问题 12 至 15 基于你刚听到的短文。

transcript.text: Question 12.
transcript.translation: 问题 12。

transcript.text: Why do new tech products soon become waste?
transcript.translation: 新的科技产品为什么很快就变成垃圾？

transcript.text: Question 13.
transcript.translation: 问题 13。

transcript.text: What did the French government require tech companies to do to help consumers make better choices?
transcript.translation: 为帮助消费者做出更好的选择，法国政府要求科技公司做什么？

transcript.text: Question 14.
transcript.translation: 问题 14。

transcript.text: What should tech companies do to help ensure environmental sustainability?
transcript.translation: 为帮助确保环境可持续性，科技公司应当做什么？

transcript.text: Question 15.
transcript.translation: 问题 15。

transcript.text: What does the speaker think of the problem of waste?
transcript.translation: 说话者如何看待垃圾问题？

questions.questionText: Why do new tech products soon become waste?

options.label: A
options.text: Consumers often have a craving for the latest model.

options.label: B
options.text: Such products tend to comprise parts that are irreplaceable.

options.label: C
options.text: Tech firms intentionally design products to have short lifespans.

options.label: D
options.text: Manufacturers use effective strategies to promote fancier products.

questions.analysis: 原文「technology firms often purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired, so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one」，purposely design... will not last long 即刻意设计成寿命短，故选 C。B 只截取了「无法维修」这一半，且 irreplaceable 属过度引申。

questions.questionText: What did the French government require tech companies to do to help consumers make better choices?

options.label: A
options.text: Indicate the competitiveness of their products.

options.label: B
options.text: List a repairability score of their products.

options.label: C
options.text: Specify the major parts of their products.

options.label: D
options.text: Detail the life cycle of their products.

questions.analysis: 原文「This year, the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score」，与 B 逐词对应；下一句也说明目的是让消费者做出更好的购买选择。故选 B。

questions.questionText: What should tech companies do to help ensure environmental sustainability?

options.label: A
options.text: Take the initiative to reduce electronic waste.

options.label: B
options.text: Take due caution in upgrading their products.

options.label: C
options.text: Invest in constructing more recycling facilities.

options.label: D
options.text: Substitute all toxic substances with non-toxic ones.

questions.analysis: 在列举电子垃圾的危害后，原文说「We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem. If they won't, governments must make them do so」，take the lead 即主动带头解决电子垃圾问题，故选 A。C 的回收设施、D 的替换有毒物质原文均未作为要求提出。

questions.questionText: What does the speaker think of the problem of waste?

options.label: A
options.text: It can be solved.

options.label: B
options.text: It is certain to worsen.

options.label: C
options.text: It will be fixed by tech companies.

options.label: D
options.text: It is unavoidable in the long run.

questions.analysis: 结尾「In this world, damage is a certainty, but we cannot leave things broken. A problem of our creation is a problem that can be fixed」，明确表示这是可以解决的问题，故选 A。C 的「将由科技公司解决」与原文「若它们不做，政府必须迫使其做」的条件语气不符。

transcript.text: Recording 1.
transcript.translation: 录音一。

transcript.text: On average, US workers spend about 10% of their workday surfing the internet, emailing friends or shopping online.
transcript.translation: 美国员工平均把大约百分之十的工作时间花在上网、给朋友发邮件或网购上。

transcript.text: This behaviour, called cyberloafing, is believed to cost employers up to $85 billion a year in lost productivity.
transcript.translation: 这种被称为「网络摸鱼」的行为，据信每年让雇主损失高达 850 亿美元的生产力。

transcript.text: The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behaviour through interventions such as internet monitoring and computer use policies.
transcript.translation: 大多数关于网络摸鱼的研究，关注的是如何通过网络监控、电脑使用规定等干预手段来阻止员工做出这种行为。

transcript.text: But it turns out such behaviour may not be a sign that a worker is lazy or just wasting time.
transcript.translation: 但事实表明，这种行为未必说明员工懒惰或只是在浪费时间。

transcript.text: Social media use at work has been linked to higher levels of employee engagement and job satisfaction.
transcript.translation: 工作中使用社交媒体已被发现与更高的员工投入度和工作满意度相关。

transcript.text: New research suggests cyberloafing could help workers cope with an exceptionally stressful work environment.
transcript.translation: 新的研究表明，网络摸鱼可能有助于员工应对压力极大的工作环境。

transcript.text: But is cyberloafing actually effective at reducing employee stress levels?
transcript.translation: 但网络摸鱼真的能有效降低员工的压力水平吗？

transcript.text: That's the question my research team wanted to answer in our new study.
transcript.translation: 这正是我的研究团队在新研究中想要回答的问题。

transcript.text: Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations.
transcript.translation: 我们的假设是，网络摸鱼可以充当一种短暂的休息，让员工有机会从压力大的工作情境中恢复过来。

transcript.text: To test this, we asked workers to complete an online survey and rank how much time they spent cyberloafing, checking non-work emails and shopping.
transcript.translation: 为了验证这一点，我们请员工填写一份在线问卷，对自己花在网络摸鱼、查看非工作邮件和购物上的时间进行评估。

transcript.text: We also asked them to rank job satisfaction, their desire to quit and how often they've experienced mistreatment at work, such as being bullied, threatened or yelled at.
transcript.translation: 我们还请他们对工作满意度、离职意愿以及在职场遭受不公对待（比如被欺负、威胁或呵斥）的频率进行评分。

transcript.text: As you might expect, we found that overall, more mistreatment at work was correlated with lower levels of job satisfaction and a greater desire to quit.
transcript.translation: 正如你可能预料到的，我们发现总体而言，职场中遭受的不公对待越多，工作满意度越低，离职意愿越强。

transcript.text: More interestingly, we found that cyberloafing effectively buffered this connection.
transcript.translation: 更有意思的是，我们发现网络摸鱼有效地缓冲了这种关联。

transcript.text: That is, mistreated workers who spent more time surfing the web and checking emails reported higher job satisfaction and were less likely to want to quit than similar participants who didn't cyberloaf as much.
transcript.translation: 也就是说，与摸鱼较少的同类参与者相比，那些遭受不公对待但花更多时间上网和查邮件的员工，工作满意度更高，离职意愿也更低。

transcript.text: This suggests that cyberloafing acts as a sort of relief valve for workers, helping them recover from stressful experiences.
transcript.translation: 这表明网络摸鱼对员工而言相当于一个减压阀，帮助他们从有压力的经历中恢复。

transcript.text: While we did not directly assess how cyberloafing affects worker performance, we believe by relieving stress, it may not only reduce worker turnover but also ultimately bolster productivity.
transcript.translation: 虽然我们没有直接评估网络摸鱼如何影响员工绩效，但我们认为，通过缓解压力，它不仅可能降低员工流失率，最终还可能提升生产率。

transcript.text: This fits with other recent research that suggests taking short breaks is associated with higher levels of daily job performance.
transcript.translation: 这与近期另一些研究的结论一致：短暂休息与更高的日常工作绩效相关。

transcript.text: That isn't to say cyberloafing is always good.
transcript.translation: 这并不是说网络摸鱼总是好事。

transcript.text: Too much time spent on non-work activities likely causes performance to suffer.
transcript.translation: 在非工作活动上花太多时间很可能会损害绩效。

transcript.text: All in all, managers should be more lenient with employees.
transcript.translation: 总的来说，管理者对员工应当更宽容一些。

transcript.text: We believe a bit of online shopping or surfing the internet at work could make workers more productive in the long run.
transcript.translation: 我们认为，在工作中稍微网购或上上网，从长远看能让员工更有效率。

transcript.translation: 问题 16 至 18 基于你刚听到的录音。

transcript.text: Question 16.
transcript.translation: 问题 16。

transcript.text: Question 17.
transcript.translation: 问题 17。

transcript.text: What was the hypothesis of the speaker's research team?
transcript.translation: 说话者研究团队的假设是什么？

transcript.text: Question 18.
transcript.translation: 问题 18。

transcript.text: On what point do the results of the speaker's study agree with other recent research?
transcript.translation: 说话者研究的结果在哪一点上与近期其他研究一致？

questions.questionText: What does most cyberloafing research focus on?

options.label: A
options.text: How internet monitoring can be implemented.

options.label: B
options.text: How to encourage productive internet surfing.

options.label: C
options.text: How cyberloafing affects overall productivity.

options.label: D
options.text: How to prevent employees from cyberloafing.

questions.analysis: 原文「The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behaviour through interventions such as internet monitoring and computer use policies」，即多数研究关注如何阻止员工上班摸鱼，故选 D。A 的网络监控只是干预手段之一，不是研究焦点本身。

questions.questionText: What was the hypothesis of the speaker's research team?

options.label: A
options.text: Cyberloafing is a sign of workers' laziness.

options.label: B
options.text: Cyberloafing may relieve employees of stress.

options.label: C
options.text: Employee engagement is closely related to job satisfaction.

options.label: D
options.text: Overuse of social media may lead to decline in productivity.

questions.analysis: 原文「Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations」，即摸鱼可作为短暂休息帮助员工从压力中恢复，故选 B。A 是研究要推翻的旧看法（such behaviour may not be a sign that a worker is lazy）。

questions.questionText: On what point do the results of the speaker's study agree with other recent research?

options.label: A
options.text: Taking mini-breaks means better job performance.

options.label: B
options.text: Cyberloafing generally does more harm than good.

options.label: C
options.text: Worker turnover is linked to the time allowed for cyberloafing.

options.label: D
options.text: Employees who indulge in internet surfing are most likely to quit.

questions.analysis: 原文「This fits with other recent research that suggests taking short breaks is associated with higher levels of daily job performance」，fits with 即与其他新近研究一致之处，内容是短暂休息与更高工作绩效相关，故选 A。B、D 与研究结论相反。

transcript.text: Recording 2.
transcript.translation: 录音二。

transcript.text: When Julius Morton moved to Nebraska City in 1854, he faced a problem shared by many settlers in the territory.
transcript.translation: 1854 年朱利叶斯·莫顿搬到内布拉斯加城时，他面临着该地区许多定居者共同的问题。

transcript.text: It was a treeless plain.
transcript.translation: 那是一片没有树木的平原。

transcript.text: That meant no trees for building materials, or for fuel.
transcript.translation: 这意味着没有树木可作建筑材料，也没有树木可作燃料。

transcript.text: But Morton was one of the world's first conservationists, stating, For prosperity, we ought to plant as many forests as we have exhausted and consumed.
transcript.translation: 但莫顿是世界上最早的环保主义者之一，他表示：为了繁荣，我们消耗掉多少森林，就应当种回多少森林。

transcript.text: So he started planting trees, beginning with his own land.
transcript.translation: 于是他开始种树，先从自己的土地种起。

transcript.text: By 1860, Morton possessed a forest of more than 300 trees.
transcript.translation: 到 1860 年，莫顿已拥有一片三百多棵树的树林。

transcript.text: A few years later, he had more than 1,000.
transcript.translation: 几年之后，他种下的树超过了一千棵。

transcript.text: As the forests grew, so did Morton's influence in Nebraska.
transcript.translation: 随着林木不断长大，莫顿在内布拉斯加州的影响力也随之增长。

transcript.text: This was largely because Morton founded the Nebraska City News, the state's first newspaper, in which he frequently wrote editorials about the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting.
transcript.translation: 这在很大程度上是因为莫顿创办了该州第一份报纸《内布拉斯加城新闻报》，并经常在报上撰写社论，阐述植树在实用和审美方面的好处。

transcript.text: He also organized the Nebraska State Gardening Society and served on the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture.
transcript.translation: 他还组建了内布拉斯加州园艺协会，并在该州农业委员会任职。

transcript.text: While serving on the board, Morton came up with an idea to spread his belief in tree planting statewide.
transcript.translation: 在委员会任职期间，莫顿想出了一个把植树理念推广到全州的办法。

transcript.text: On January 4, 1872, Morton drafted a resolution that April 10 be designated Day for the Planting of Trees in the State of Nebraska, and urged people to go out and plant trees themselves.
transcript.translation: 1872 年 1 月 4 日，莫顿起草了一项决议，提议将 4 月 10 日定为内布拉斯加州植树日，并号召人们走出家门亲手植树。

transcript.text: Morton called the special event Arbor Day, as arbor is Latin for tree.
transcript.translation: 莫顿把这个特别的日子称为 Arbor Day，因为 arbor 在拉丁语中意为「树」。

transcript.text: The state government agreed, and on April 10, 1872, the first unofficial Arbor Day was celebrated throughout Nebraska.
transcript.translation: 州政府表示同意，1872 年 4 月 10 日，第一个非官方的植树节在内布拉斯加州各地举行。

transcript.text: Prizes were awarded to counties, cities, and individuals who planted the largest number of trees.
transcript.translation: 植树数量最多的县、市和个人都获得了奖励。

transcript.text: That day, an astounding 1 million trees were planted in Nebraska, an average of more than six for every man, woman, and child in the state.
transcript.translation: 那一天，内布拉斯加州种下了惊人的一百万棵树，相当于全州每位男女老少平均种了六棵以上。

transcript.text: Since 1885, Nebraska has planted more than 700,000 acres of trees, earning it the nickname the Tree Planter's State.
transcript.translation: 自 1885 年以来，内布拉斯加州已植树逾七十万英亩，因而获得了「植树者之州」的绰号。

transcript.text: Arbor Day became a legal civic holiday in the state in 1885.
transcript.translation: 1885 年，植树节成为该州法定的公民假日。

transcript.text: It was held on April 22, Julius Morton's birthday.
transcript.translation: 节日定在 4 月 22 日，也就是朱利叶斯·莫顿的生日。

transcript.text: In addition to a parade in Nebraska City, Morton introduced what has since become a long-standing Arbor Day tradition.
transcript.translation: 除了在内布拉斯加城举行游行外，莫顿还开创了一项此后长期延续的植树节传统。

transcript.text: Schoolchildren went outside and planted trees together.
transcript.translation: 学童们走到户外，一起种树。

transcript.text: In 1970, nearly a century after Arbor Day was first celebrated, President Richard Nixon declared the last Friday of every April to be observed as National Arbor Day.
transcript.translation: 1970 年，也就是首次庆祝植树节将近一个世纪之后，理查德·尼克松总统宣布将每年 4 月的最后一个星期五定为全国植树节。

transcript.text: All 50 states recognize the April observance, although many hold an additional State Arbor Day in a month more suited to local tree planting.
transcript.translation: 全部五十个州都承认这一四月的节日，不过许多州还会在更适合当地植树的月份另设一个州植树节。

transcript.translation: 问题 19 至 21 基于你刚听到的录音。

transcript.text: Question 19.
transcript.translation: 问题 19。

transcript.text: What does the speaker say about Nebraska City in 1854 when Julius Morton moved there?
transcript.translation: 关于 1854 年朱利叶斯·莫顿搬去时的内布拉斯加城，说话者说了什么？

transcript.text: Question 20.
transcript.translation: 问题 20。

transcript.text: What did Julius Morton do that increased his influence in Nebraska City?
transcript.translation: 朱利叶斯·莫顿做了什么，使他在内布拉斯加城的影响力得以提升？

transcript.text: Question 21.
transcript.translation: 问题 21。

transcript.text: What does the speaker say happened on April 10, 1872?
transcript.translation: 说话者说 1872 年 4 月 10 日发生了什么？

questions.questionText: What does the speaker say about Nebraska City in 1854 when Julius Morton moved there?

options.label: A
options.text: There were no wooden buildings.

options.label: B
options.text: There were environmental problems.

options.label: C
options.text: There were no trees.

options.label: D
options.text: There were few settlers.

questions.analysis: 原文「It was a treeless plain. That meant no trees for building materials, or for fuel」，即当时是一片没有树的平原，故选 C。A 是「没有树」导致的可能后果，但原文只说缺少建材，未说没有木屋；D 与原文 a problem shared by many settlers 相矛盾。

questions.questionText: What did Julius Morton do that increased his influence in Nebraska City?

options.label: A
options.text: He served as chairman of the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture.

options.label: B
options.text: He urged the state to start the Nebraska State Gardening Society.

options.label: C
options.text: He engaged himself in a large number of aesthetic projects.

options.label: D
options.text: He founded a newspaper and used it to promote his ideas.

questions.analysis: 原文「This was largely because Morton founded the Nebraska City News, the state's first newspaper, in which he frequently wrote editorials about the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting」，即办报并借此宣传植树主张，故选 D。他是 served on the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture（任职），不是 chairman；园艺协会是他 organized 的，不是敦促州政府创办。

questions.questionText: What does the speaker say happened on April 10, 1872?

options.label: A
options.text: A special prize was awarded to Julius Morton.

options.label: B
options.text: One million trees were planted throughout Nebraska.

options.label: C
options.text: The state government declared it the official Arbor Day.

options.label: D
options.text: Nebraska earned the nickname "the Tree Planters State".

questions.analysis: 原文「on April 10, 1872, the first unofficial Arbor Day was celebrated throughout Nebraska... That day, an astounding 1 million trees were planted in Nebraska」，故选 B。C 错在当天是 unofficial（非官方）；D 的绰号来自 1885 年后累计植树 70 万英亩；奖项是发给各县、市和个人，不是发给莫顿本人。

transcript.text: Recording 3.
transcript.translation: 录音三。

transcript.text: Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago.
transcript.translation: 现代人类大约在二十万年前起源于非洲。

transcript.text: They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago.
transcript.translation: 随后在距今六万年之后的某个时候，他们扩散到欧洲和亚洲各地。

transcript.text: This is the out-of-Africa model, as it's commonly known.
transcript.translation: 这就是人们通常所说的「走出非洲」模型。

transcript.text: In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance, but this popular idea is in need of revision, particularly given the number of important findings across Asia over the past few decades.
transcript.translation: 20 世纪 90 年代，这一假说被广泛接受，但这个流行的观点需要修正，尤其是考虑到过去几十年间亚洲各地的大量重要发现。

transcript.text: For instance, many new human fossils found, particularly in China, are now dated as older than 60,000 years.
transcript.translation: 例如，新发现的许多人类化石——尤其是在中国发现的——如今测定的年代都早于六万年。

transcript.text: This calls into question the idea that modern humans migrated out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
transcript.translation: 这就对「现代人类直到六万年前才走出非洲」这一观点提出了质疑。

transcript.text: Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna Cave in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
transcript.translation: 以近期在中国广西壮族自治区娄洞发现的两颗现代人牙齿为例。

transcript.text: When my research team and I dated these teeth, we found they were more than 70,000 years old, a situation clearly impossible if modern humans moved out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
transcript.translation: 当我和研究团队对这两颗牙齿进行年代测定时，发现它们已有七万多年历史；如果现代人类六万年前才走出非洲，这种情况显然不可能出现。

transcript.text: So with such findings, what happened exactly?
transcript.translation: 那么面对这些发现，究竟发生了什么？

transcript.text: Where does the most current data suggest we came from?
transcript.translation: 最新的数据表明我们究竟来自哪里？

transcript.text: The first question we should ask is, why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with?
transcript.translation: 我们首先该问的问题是：现代人类当初为什么要离开非洲？

transcript.text: If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change.
transcript.translation: 如果一个种群完全适应了某个特定环境，并且能够获得充足的资源，那么它其实没有理由迁移或改变。

transcript.text: For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them.
transcript.translation: 例如，非洲的一些猴子，其牙齿在数百万年间几乎没有变化，这表明它们找到了一处适合自己的地方。

transcript.text: So what happened with humans?
transcript.translation: 那么人类身上发生了什么？

transcript.text: Some researchers have suggested that population density increased to the point where smaller human groups were forced to explore new lands.
transcript.translation: 一些研究者认为，人口密度增长到了迫使较小的人群去开拓新土地的程度。

transcript.text: Other researchers have suggested that due to major environmental events in East Africa, humans were prompted to find greener pastures.
transcript.translation: 另一些研究者认为，由于东非发生了重大的环境事件，人类被迫去寻找更肥美的土地。

transcript.text: Yet another explanation could simply be that early modern human hunters were following the large animals that they relied on, and so they moved out of Africa without realising that they were actually moving from one continent to another.
transcript.translation: 还有一种解释可能仅仅是：早期现代人猎手在追随他们赖以为生的大型动物，于是走出了非洲，却没有意识到自己其实正从一个大陆迁往另一个大陆。

transcript.text: Humans need daily access to reliable fresh water, which appears to be absent from many coastal areas.
transcript.translation: 人类每天都需要可靠的淡水，而许多沿海地区似乎并不具备这一条件。

transcript.text: This brings us to another question, by which route did modern humans move out of Africa?
transcript.translation: 这就引出了另一个问题：现代人类是沿哪条路线走出非洲的？

transcript.text: No clear routes across the Mediterranean from North Africa appear to be present.
transcript.translation: 从北非跨越地中海的路线似乎并不明确存在。

transcript.text: So the earlier dispersals out of Africa and into Europe and Asia might have been across the Arabian Peninsula.
transcript.translation: 因此，早期走出非洲、进入欧洲和亚洲的扩散过程，可能是经由阿拉伯半岛完成的。

transcript.text: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
transcript.translation: 问题 22 至 25 基于你刚听到的录音。

transcript.text: Question 22.
transcript.translation: 问题 22。

transcript.text: What do we learn about modern humans according to the hypothesis commonly accepted in the 1990s?
transcript.translation: 根据 20 世纪 90 年代被广泛接受的假说，我们对现代人类有什么了解？

transcript.text: Question 23.
transcript.translation: 问题 23。

transcript.text: What has called into question the out-of-Africa model?
transcript.translation: 是什么对「走出非洲」模型提出了质疑？

transcript.text: Question 24.
transcript.translation: 问题 24。

transcript.text: What does the speaker want to show with the example of some monkeys in Africa?
transcript.translation: 说话者想用非洲一些猴子的例子说明什么？

transcript.translation: 说话者在讲话接近尾声时提出了什么问题？

questions.questionText: What do we learn about modern humans according to the hypothesis commonly accepted in the 1990s?

options.label: A
options.text: They spread across Europe and Asia in a few decades.

options.label: B
options.text: They lived mostly in Africa for about 200,000 years.

options.label: C
options.text: They preferred to live in Europe rather than in Asia.

options.label: D
options.text: They moved out of Africa about 60,000 years ago.

questions.analysis: 原文介绍「走出非洲」模型：现代人约 20 万年前起源于非洲，「They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago」，并说该假说在 1990 年代被广泛接受，故选 D。B 错在现代人是 6 万年前之后才离开非洲，并非在非洲生活了 20 万年。

questions.questionText: What has called into question the out-of-Africa model?

options.label: A
options.text: The discovery of two modern human teeth in China.

options.label: B
options.text: The traces of human migration out of Africa to Asia.

options.label: C
options.text: The human fossils discovered most recently in Africa.

options.label: D
options.text: The Luna cave in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

questions.analysis: 原文说在中国发现的许多新化石年代早于 6 万年，「This calls into question the idea that modern humans migrated out of Africa only 60,000 years ago」，随即举例广西娄洞发现的两颗现代人牙齿经测定超过 7 万年，若 6 万年前才走出非洲则不可能，故选 A。C 错在化石发现于亚洲（中国）而非非洲；D 只是发现地点，本身不构成质疑。

questions.questionText: What does the speaker want to show with the example of some monkeys in Africa?

options.label: A
options.text: There must have been some reason for human migration.

options.label: B
options.text: There have been changes in animals' living conditions.

options.label: C
options.text: Humans adapted themselves to the environment there.

options.label: D
options.text: Humans had access to abundant food sources there.

questions.analysis: 举例前提出「If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change」，猴子牙齿数百万年几乎未变正说明它们找到了合适的栖息地。以此反推：人类既然迁徙，必定另有原因，下文随即列举人口密度、环境事件、追随猎物等解释。故选 A。

questions.questionText: What question does the speaker raise close to the end of the talk?

options.label: A
options.text: How humans settled down on the Arabian Peninsula.

options.label: B
options.text: When modern humans started to disperse out of Africa.

options.label: C
options.text: What path modern humans took to migrate out of Africa.

options.label: D
options.text: Why fresh water is so important for human survival.

questions.analysis: 结尾处「This brings us to another question, by which route did modern humans move out of Africa?」，by which route 即迁徙路线，对应 C 的 what path。随后提到跨地中海没有明确路线、可能取道阿拉伯半岛，也是围绕路线展开。B 的时间问题在讲话开头已交代。

questionGroups.title: Section A

paragraphs.text: You might not know yourself as well as you think. According to a new study, people are __26__ accurate judges of only some of their behaviors. While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long-term personality traits, this new study __27__ how well people understand how they are acting from one moment to the next. Researchers asked participants to wear audio recorders that automatically __28__ every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m. to record 30 seconds of audio. These participants were then emailed surveys four times a day asking them to __29__ how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day. The study used data from 248 participants, all of whom answered questions about their behavior for two __30__ weeks and wore the audio device for one of those weeks.
paragraphs.translation: 你可能并不像自己以为的那样了解自己。一项新研究表明，人们只对自己的部分行为做出相对准确的判断。以往关于人们自我认知程度的研究大多针对长期的人格特质，而这项新研究探究的是人们对自己此刻行为方式的理解程度。研究人员要求参与者佩戴录音设备，该设备在早上 7 点到凌晨 2 点之间每隔 9.5 分钟自动启动一次，录下 30 秒的音频。随后研究人员每天四次通过邮件向这些参与者发送问卷，请他们回想自己在当天某个特定时段内表现得有多外向、多随和、多尽责。该研究采用了 248 名参与者的数据，所有人都就自己连续两周的行为回答了问题，并在其中一周佩戴了录音设备。

paragraphs.text: Six laboratory assistants rated each participant's audio clips to see how their observations compared with people's __31__ of themselves. The six assistants were generally in agreement with one another about how the people they were observing acted. Further, participants' ratings of their own behaviors agreed with observers' for how outgoing and how conscientious they were being. But the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness. Some of this __32__ could be because the observers used only audio clips, and thus could not read __33__ like body language, but there are __34__ other explanations, as people should be able to hear when a participant is being kind versus being rude. The weak agreement between how participants thought they were acting and what observers heard could be because people would rather __35__ rude behavior.
paragraphs.translation: 六名实验室助理对每位参与者的音频片段进行评分，以比较他们的观察结果与参与者的自我评价。这六名助理对所观察对象的行为表现看法基本一致。此外，在外向程度和尽责程度上，参与者对自身行为的评分与观察者的评分是吻合的。但在随和度这一项上，参与者与外部观察者之间的一致性要低得多。这种差异部分可能是因为观察者只依据音频片段，因而无法读取肢体语言之类的线索，但也很可能存在其他解释，因为一个人是友善还是无礼，光靠听应该也能听出来。参与者自认为的行为方式与观察者所听到的之间一致性偏低，原因可能在于人们更倾向于否认自己的无礼行为。

questionGroups.directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.

questions.analysis: 空格位于系动词 are 与形容词 accurate 之间，需副词作程度修饰。全文基调是「人们对自己的了解没有想象中好，只在部分行为上判断得还算准」，relatively accurate（相对准确）恰好呼应 only some of their behaviors 的限定。probably 表推测可能性，与 only some 的对比语义不符。故选 L。
主语 this new study 为第三人称单数，空格后接 how 引导的宾语从句，需及物动词。probes 意为「探究、深入调查」，与 study 搭配自然，且与前半句 most previous studies... have been done on 构成新旧研究对象的对比。articulates 意为「清晰表达」，主语通常为人，不搭配研究探究某问题。故选 I。
定语从句主语是 audio recorders，谓语被副词 automatically 修饰，后接时间状语 every 9.5 minutes，说明录音设备每隔 9.5 分钟自动「启动」一次录音。activated 作不及物用法表示设备被激活/启动，符合语境。terminate（终止）与后文 to record 30 seconds of audio 的目的相矛盾。故选 A。
asking them to __ 后接不定式动词原形，宾语从句为 how outgoing... they were during a particular hour of the day，时间是「当天某个已过去的时段」，因此是让参与者「回想」当时的表现。recall 正合此意。deny（否认）与问卷调查的语境不符。故选 K。
空格在数词 two 与名词 weeks 之间，需形容词。后文 wore the audio device for one of those weeks 说明这两周是一段完整、前后相接的时间，consecutive weeks（连续两周）符合实验设计的表述习惯。random（随机的）与 two...weeks 的固定时段冲突。故选 D。
空格在所有格 people's 之后、介词 of 之前，需名词。句意为把助理的观察结果与「人们对自己的评价」相比较，与前文 rated each participant's audio clips 中的 rated 相呼应。assessment 意为评价、评估，正确。symptoms（症状）属医学语境，不搭配。故选 C。
Some of this __ 指代上一句 the agreement... was much smaller for agreeableness 所描述的现象，即自评与他评之间的「不一致」。discrepancy 正指这种差异，且为不可数用法与 some of this 搭配得当。故选 G。
could not read __ like body language 中，like body language 是对空格所指事物的举例，肢体语言属于非言语「线索」。read cues 是固定搭配，意为读取线索。观察者只能听音频，自然读不到这类线索。故选 E。
there are __ other explanations 中空格修饰整个存在句，表推测语气，且后接 as 引导的原因从句说明「善意还是无礼光靠听也能分辨」，即前一种解释并不充分，很可能另有原因。probably 表可能性，符合。relatively 已用于 26 题，且不修饰 there are 结构。故选 H。
would rather 后接动词原形，宾语是 rude behavior。段末解释自评与他评在随和度上差异大的原因：人们宁愿「否认」自己的无礼行为，即倾向于美化自我。deny 符合逻辑。terminate（终止）虽为动词原形，但与 would rather 表主观倾向的语义不通顺。故选 F。

questionGroups.title: Why We Need Tiny Colleges

paragraphs.text: We're experiencing the rebirth of smallness. Farmers markets, tiny homes, and brew pubs all exemplify our love of smallness. So do charter schools, coffee shops, and local bookstores. Small is often (but not always) more affordable, healthier, and sustainable, but its finest characteristic, the one that turns charm into love, is that going small allows us to be more fully who we are.
paragraphs.translation: 我们正在经历「小」的复兴。农夫市集、小房子、精酿酒吧都体现了我们对小的偏爱。特许学校、咖啡馆和本地书店也是如此。小往往（但并非总是）更便宜、更健康、更可持续，但它最可贵的特质——那个把好感变成热爱的特质——在于选择「小」能让我们更充分地做自己。

paragraphs.text: In higher education the trend is mostly in the opposite direction: Universities with 20,000 or 30,000 students are considered "mid-sized". The nation's largest university, Arizona State University, has 80,000 students on campus and aims to enroll another 100,000 students online. At the other end of the spectrum is a handful of colleges that have fewer than a hundred students on campus and no online courses: colleges such as Sterling College, Thomas More College of Liberal Arts, and Deep Springs College. These colleges are so small that they can only be called "tiny."
paragraphs.translation: 在高等教育领域，趋势基本是反方向的：拥有两三万名学生的大学被视为「中等规模」。全美最大的大学亚利桑那州立大学校园内有 8 万名学生，还计划再招收 10 万名在线学生。处在另一端的是少数校园学生不足百人、且不开设在线课程的学院，比如斯特林学院、托马斯莫尔文理学院和深泉学院。这些学院小到只能被称为「微型」。

paragraphs.text: Tiny colleges focus not just on a young person's intellect, but on the young person as a whole. Equally important, tiny colleges ask, "How can education contribute to human flourishing and the well-being of the world?" And they shape a college experience to address that question. They replace concerns about institutional growth with attention to the growth of students as fully developed participants in their communities.
paragraphs.translation: 微型学院关注的不只是年轻人的智力，而是作为整体的这个年轻人。同样重要的是，微型学院会追问：「教育如何促进人的繁荣与世界的福祉？」并围绕这个问题来塑造大学体验。它们把对机构扩张的关切，替换为对学生成长为社区中健全参与者的关注。

paragraphs.text: I've had the privilege of teaching at three different institutions of higher learning during my career — a small liberal arts college and two mid-sized public universities. I've also been profoundly disappointed in each of these institutions, and in many of my colleagues, especially when it comes to helping students and preparing them for the many responsibilities of adulthood. Administrators focus on the business of running a university, and most faculty focus on their scholarship and teaching their discipline. Little deliberate attention is given to how students mature as individuals and social beings.
paragraphs.translation: 在我的职业生涯中，我有幸在三所不同的高等院校任教——一所小型文理学院和两所中等规模的公立大学。我对这三所学校以及许多同事都深感失望，尤其是在帮助学生、让他们为成年后的诸多责任做准备这一点上。管理者专注于办大学这门生意，多数教师专注于自己的学术研究和本学科教学。几乎没人刻意关注学生如何作为独立个体和社会人而成熟起来。

paragraphs.text: Having just retired from teaching at a public university, I'm now returning to my hometown of Flagstaff, Arizona, to establish a tiny college — Flagstaff College. I'm convinced there's a need for another type of education, one devoted to helping students come into their own and into this beautiful and troubled world. Young people need an education that will provide them with meaning, hope, courage, and passion, as well as information and skills. Large institutions, I believe, are particularly ill-suited to this type of education.
paragraphs.translation: 刚从一所公立大学的教职上退休，我现在要回到家乡亚利桑那州的弗拉格斯塔夫，创办一所微型学院——弗拉格斯塔夫学院。我确信人们需要另一种教育，一种致力于帮助学生成为自己、并融入这个既美好又充满问题的世界的教育。年轻人需要的教育，除了知识和技能之外，还应给予他们意义、希望、勇气与热情。我认为，大型院校尤其不适合提供这类教育。

paragraphs.text: There's no "best of" list when it comes to tiny colleges, at least not yet. But around the country people are creating new colleges that provide an alternative to small liberal arts colleges, large public universities, and online education.
paragraphs.translation: 说到微型学院，目前还没有什么「最佳榜单」。但全美各地都有人在创办新的学院，为小型文理学院、大型公立大学和在线教育提供另一种选择。

paragraphs.text: With only 26 students, Deep Springs is the smallest college in the country and, quite likely, the most atypical (非典型的). Located on a working cattle ranch on the California-Nevada border, Deep Springs is a private, residential, two-year college for men, committed to educating students for "a life of service to humanity." Founded by the electricity tycoon (大亨) L. L. Nunn in 1917, Deep Springs' "curriculum" revolves around academics, labor, and self-governance. In addition to their courses, students are charged with running the 155-acre ranch and overseeing the functioning of the college. Students chair both the admissions and the curriculum committees.
paragraphs.translation: 深泉学院只有 26 名学生，是全美最小的学院，也很可能是最非典型的一所。它坐落在加州与内华达州交界处一座仍在运营的养牛牧场上，是一所私立、寄宿、两年制的男子学院，致力于培养学生过「服务于人类的一生」。深泉学院由电力大亨 L. L. 纳恩于 1917 年创办，其「课程」围绕学术、劳动与自治展开。除了上课，学生还负责经营这片 155 英亩的牧场并监督学院运转。招生委员会和课程委员会都由学生担任主席。

paragraphs.text: "Living in close community with one's teachers and fellow students, and being forced to take on adult responsibilities, makes for one's growth as a person," says William Hunt, who graduated last year. "To exist for very long in a community like that, you have to get over the question of whether you're sufficiently talented or principled and get started worrying about how you can stretch yourself and your peers, how much you can manage to learn with them."
paragraphs.translation: 去年毕业的威廉·亨特说：「与老师和同学紧密地生活在一个共同体中，被迫承担成年人的责任，这会促进一个人的成长。」「要在这样的共同体里长久待下去，你必须越过『我是否足够有才华、足够有原则』这个问题，转而开始琢磨如何拓展自己和同伴的边界，能和他们一起学到多少东西。」

paragraphs.text: Sterling College, in Craftsbury Common, Vermont, is also very small — fewer than 100 students. Unlike Deep Springs, Sterling focuses its curriculum on environmental and social justice issues, but like Deep Springs it places a high value on personal responsibility and manual labor. According to its catalog, a college education at Sterling combines "rigorous academics, roll-up-your-sleeves challenges, and good old hard work."
paragraphs.translation: 位于佛蒙特州克拉夫茨伯里康芒的斯特林学院同样很小——学生不足 100 人。与深泉学院不同，斯特林的课程聚焦环境与社会正义议题，但和深泉一样高度重视个人责任与体力劳动。据其课程目录介绍，在斯特林接受的大学教育融合了「严格的学术训练、需要撸起袖子面对的挑战，以及地地道道的辛苦劳作」。

paragraphs.text: The average tuition at a small liberal-arts college is $30,000 to $40,000 a year, not including the cost of living on campus, as compared to $8,000 to $10,000 a year for tuition alone at a public university. Of the tiny colleges, only Deep Springs doesn't charge tuition or room and board; students pay only for books and the cost of traveling to and from college. If tiny schools are to become a player on the higher education scene, they will need to find a way to be truly affordable.
paragraphs.translation: 小型文理学院的平均学费为每年 3 万至 4 万美元，还不含在校生活费；相比之下，公立大学仅学费为每年 8000 至 1 万美元。在这些微型学院中，只有深泉学院不收学费和食宿费，学生只需承担书本费和往返学校的路费。微型学校若要在高等教育舞台上占据一席之地，就必须找到真正让人负担得起的办法。

paragraphs.text: Doing so may not be that difficult so long as they do not pattern themselves too closely on existing norms. We've come to believe that a good college should have many academic programs and excellent facilities, posh (豪华的) dorms, an array of athletic programs, and a world-class student activity center. Imagine a good college without a climbing wall! We also have accepted the idea that college presidents, and their many vice-presidents, should be paid like their counterparts in the business world and that higher education requires an elaborate, up-to-date technology infrastructure. All of this drives up the cost of education.
paragraphs.translation: 只要不过分照搬现有的模式，做到这一点也许并不那么难。我们已经习惯于认为，一所好大学应当有众多学科专业和一流设施、豪华宿舍、种类繁多的体育项目，以及世界一流的学生活动中心。想象一下一所没有攀岩墙的好大学！我们还接受了这样的观念：大学校长及其麾下众多副校长的薪酬应当向商界同行看齐，高等教育需要一套复杂而先进的技术基础设施。所有这些都推高了教育成本。

paragraphs.text: The "trick" to making tiny colleges affordable, if that's the right word, is simplicity. At its core, education is a human-to-human interaction. Reflecting on his own college education, President Garfield once commented that an ideal college would consist of nothing more than the legendary teacher Mark Hopkins on one end of a log and a student on the other. The economics of a tiny college, in other words, might be similar to that of a tiny house. Because it is small, a tiny house costs less to build and less to furnish, insure, and maintain. But the economic benefits of a small house don't end there. Tiny homes discourage homeowners from buying stuff that they really don't need, because there's no place to put it.
paragraphs.translation: 让微型学院变得负担得起的「诀窍」——如果这个词用得恰当的话——就是简单。教育的核心是人与人之间的互动。加菲尔德总统在回顾自己的大学教育时曾评论说，理想的大学不过是一根圆木，一端坐着传奇教师马克·霍普金斯，另一端坐着一名学生。换句话说，微型学院的经济学也许类似于小房子的经济学。因为小，小房子建造成本更低，装修、投保和维护的花费也更少。而小房子的经济好处还不止于此：因为没地方放，它会让屋主打消购买那些其实并不需要的东西的念头。

paragraphs.text: I'm a late convert to the idea of tiny colleges, and I fully understand the need for many diverse types of educational institutions. Academic research and job training are important, but tiny colleges aren't suited for either. The educational needs of a complex society are themselves complex, and no single model can meet all of these needs. But I'm now convinced there's an educational need that's now going almost completely unmet: namely, the need to help young people transition into adulthood. Tiny colleges can do this better than any other type of educational institution.
paragraphs.translation: 我是很晚才接受微型学院这一理念的，我也完全理解社会需要多种多样的教育机构。学术研究和职业培训都很重要，但微型学院两者都不擅长。复杂社会的教育需求本身就是复杂的，没有哪一种单一模式能满足全部需求。但我现在确信，有一项教育需求几乎完全没有被满足：即帮助年轻人过渡到成年阶段。在这件事上，微型学院比任何其他类型的教育机构都做得更好。

paragraphs.text: The ultimate justification for a tiny college is the conviction that each of us comes into our full humanity by close interaction with those who know and care for us, and that one of the basic purposes of higher education is social. Although we give lip service to the idea that a college education will make us better people, when all's said and done, we think of higher education primarily in economic terms. We've come to think of higher education as a means to make a living rather than make a life. We've also come to see higher education as a private good rather than a public one. Tiny colleges are not the answer to all of our educational requirements, but they're an answer to one of our most basic educational necessities: the need to produce thoughtful, engaged, and compassionate human beings.
paragraphs.translation: 微型学院存在的最终理由，是这样一个信念：我们每个人都是通过与了解自己、关心自己的人密切互动而成就完整人性的，而高等教育的基本目的之一就是社会性的。尽管我们嘴上认同大学教育会让我们成为更好的人，但说到底，我们主要还是从经济角度看待高等教育。我们已经把高等教育当作谋生的手段，而不是构筑人生的途径；我们也已经把高等教育视为私人物品而非公共物品。微型学院并不能解答我们全部的教育诉求，但它回应了我们最基本的教育需求之一：培养有思想、有担当、有同情心的人。

questionGroups.directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.statementText: One tiny American college situated on a cattle farm is devoted to educating students to serve mankind throughout their lives.
questions.analysis: 定位词 cattle farm、serve mankind。G 段写深泉学院「Located on a working cattle ranch on the California-Nevada border」，且「committed to educating students for 'a life of service to humanity'」，与陈述中「坐落于养牛牧场」「培养学生一生服务人类」完全对应。故选 G。

questions.statementText: Much to the author's disappointment, the three institutions of higher learning where she taught largely ignore students' growth as social beings.
questions.analysis: 定位词 three institutions、disappointment、social beings。D 段作者自述曾在三所高校任教并「profoundly disappointed in each of these institutions」，段末点明「Little deliberate attention is given to how students mature as individuals and social beings」，即忽视学生作为社会人的成长。故选 D。

questions.statementText: Tiny colleges must be made affordable in order to play a role in higher education.
questions.analysis: 定位词 affordable、play a role。J 段结尾「If tiny schools are to become a player on the higher education scene, they will need to find a way to be truly affordable」是该陈述的同义改写，become a player 对应 play a role。故选 J。

questions.statementText: According to a recent graduate from a tiny college, living together with faculty and fellow students is conducive to a student's growth as a person.
questions.analysis: 定位词 recent graduate、living together。H 段引用去年毕业的 William Hunt 的话「Living in close community with one's teachers and fellow students... makes for one's growth as a person」，makes for 对应 is conducive to。故选 H。

questions.statementText: Rather than going small, most American universities are trying to go big.
questions.analysis: 定位词 go big。B 段开篇即指出高等教育的趋势「mostly in the opposite direction」，并以两三万人算「中等规模」、亚利桑那州立大学 8 万在校生并计划再招 10 万在线学生为例，说明大学在往大里办。故选 B。

questions.statementText: In a certain tiny college, rigorous academic work and traditional manual labor are integrated.
questions.analysis: 定位词 rigorous、manual labor。I 段介绍斯特林学院「places a high value on personal responsibility and manual labor」，并引用其课程目录「combines 'rigorous academics, roll-up-your-sleeves challenges, and good old hard work'」，即严谨学术与体力劳动相结合。故选 I。

questions.statementText: Tiny colleges focus on educating students to become well-rounded citizens instead of seeking their own expansion.
questions.analysis: 定位词 well-rounded、expansion。C 段指出微型学院关注的是「the young person as a whole」，并「replace concerns about institutional growth with attention to the growth of students as fully developed participants in their communities」，institutional growth 即机构扩张。故选 C。

questions.statementText: The essence of education lies in the interaction between people.
questions.analysis: 定位词 essence、interaction。L 段第二句「At its core, education is a human-to-human interaction」即「教育的本质是人与人的互动」，at its core 对应 essence。故选 L。

questions.statementText: After her retirement, the author has decided to set up a tiny college in her hometown.
questions.analysis: 定位词 retirement、hometown。E 段开头「Having just retired from teaching at a public university, I'm now returning to my hometown of Flagstaff, Arizona, to establish a tiny college」与陈述逐项对应。故选 E。

questions.statementText: Tiny colleges are justified as it is believed that our growth into full humanity comes through interaction with people near and dear to us.
questions.analysis: 定位词 justified、full humanity。N 段首句「The ultimate justification for a tiny college is the conviction that each of us comes into our full humanity by close interaction with those who know and care for us」，those who know and care for us 即 people near and dear to us。故选 N。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: If you're someone who has turned to snacking on junk food more in the pandemic (大流行病), you're not alone. Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances. His 2013 book, Salt Sugar Fat, explored food companies' aggressive marketing of those products and their impact on our health. In his new book, Hooked, Moss updates the food giants' efforts to keep us eating what they serve, and how they're responding to complaints from consumers and health advocates.
paragraphs.translation: 如果你在大流行期间更频繁地吃起了垃圾零食，你并不孤单。调查记者迈克尔·莫斯说，加工食品是被刻意设计来让你上瘾的，这一点与酒精、香烟或其他有害物质并无二致。他 2013 年出版的《盐糖脂》一书剖析了食品公司对这些产品的激进营销及其对我们健康的影响。在新书《上钩》中，莫斯更新了食品巨头让我们持续消费其产品的种种手段，以及它们如何回应消费者与健康倡导者的批评。

paragraphs.text: Processed food is inexpensive, it's legal, and it's everywhere. Companies' advertising is cueing us to remember those products and we want those products constantly. So the food environment is one of those key things that makes food even more problematic for so many people. Memory, nostalgia (怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave. Soda companies discovered that if they put a soda in the hands of a child when they're at a ball game with their parents, that soda will forever be associated with that joyous moment. Later in life, when that child wants to experience a joyous moment, they're going to think of soda. Many people seek comfort in the snacks they remember from childhood.
paragraphs.translation: 加工食品便宜、合法，而且无处不在。企业的广告不断提示我们记住这些产品，于是我们时时刻刻都想要它们。因此，食品环境是使食品对许多人而言问题更严重的关键因素之一。记忆——尤其是怀旧——在我们所渴望的食物中扮演着重要角色。汽水公司发现，如果孩子和父母一起看球赛时手里被塞了一罐汽水，这罐汽水就会永远与那个快乐时刻联系在一起。等这个孩子长大后想重温快乐时刻，就会想到汽水。许多人从童年记忆中的零食里寻求慰藉。

paragraphs.text: Moss examines the way companies capitalize on our memories, cravings and brain chemistry to keep us snacking.
paragraphs.translation: 莫斯考察了企业如何利用我们的记忆、渴望和大脑化学机制，让我们不停地吃零食。

paragraphs.text: One of the reasons I came to think that some of these food products are even more powerful, more troublesome than drugs can be is memory. What we eat is all about memory. And we begin forming memories for food at a really early age. And we keep those memories for a lifetime. Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products. One of the features of addiction that scientists studying drug addiction discovered back in the 1990s was that the faster a substance hits the brain, the more apt we are as a result to act impulsively. There's nothing faster than food in its ability to hit the brain. For Moss, this puts the notion of "fast food" in an entirely new light as this isn't limited to fast food chains — almost 90% of food products in grocery stores are processed foods. Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging.
paragraphs.translation: 我之所以认为其中一些食品比毒品更强大、更麻烦，原因之一就是记忆。我们所吃的东西完全关乎记忆。我们在很小的年纪就开始形成关于食物的记忆，并且终生保留这些记忆。深知这一点的食品业花费大量精力去塑造我们对其产品的记忆。研究药物成瘾的科学家早在 20 世纪 90 年代就发现，成瘾的特征之一是：一种物质进入大脑的速度越快，我们越容易因此冲动行事。而在冲击大脑的速度上，没有什么比食物更快。对莫斯而言，这让「快餐」这一概念呈现出全新的含义，因为它并不局限于快餐连锁店——杂货店里近 90% 的食品都是加工食品。从生产到包装，这个行业的一切都关乎速度。

paragraphs.text: Overall, Moss outlines the industry's dependence on making their products inexpensive, super delicious, and incredibly convenient for consumers. Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods.
paragraphs.translation: 总的来说，莫斯勾勒出该行业对「让产品廉价、超级美味、极其便利」的依赖。如今越来越多的人开始在意自己吃进去的东西、想要吃得更健康，而这些公司却发现很难满足这一新需求，因为它们自己已经沉溺于制造这类方便食品。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: In what way does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes?

options.label: A
options.text: They are all addictive.

options.label: B
options.text: They are all necessary evils.

options.label: C
options.text: They are all engineered to be enjoyed.

options.label: D
options.text: They are all in increasingly great demand.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第一段指出 Michael Moss 认为「processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances」，hook 意为使上瘾，not unlike 表示「与……并无不同」，即加工食品与烟酒的共同点是让人成瘾。故选 A。
questions.keySentence: Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances.

wrongOptions.B: 文中未把加工食品称为「必要之恶」，原文强调的是成瘾性而非其必要性。
wrongOptions.C: engineered 后接的是 to hook you（使人上瘾），不是 to be enjoyed，属偷换关键词。
wrongOptions.D: 需求增长在文中并非烟酒与加工食品的类比点，且第五段说的是消费者转向更健康饮食。

questions.questionText: What does the author say plays a key role in the foods we crave?

options.label: A
options.text: The food environment.

options.label: B
options.text: Aggressive marketing.

options.label: C
options.text: Convenience

options.label: D
options.text: Memory.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第二段明确写道「Memory, nostalgia in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave」，题干中的 plays a key role 即原文 plays a big role 的同义替换，主语是 Memory。故选 D。
questions.keySentence: Memory, nostalgia (怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave.

wrongOptions.A: 食品环境在同段被称为使问题更严重的关键因素之一，但直接与 the foods we crave 搭配的是 memory。
wrongOptions.B: 激进营销是 2013 年旧书《盐糖脂》探讨的内容，并非本处所指。
wrongOptions.C: 便利性出现在末段，用于概括行业对产品的定位，与「渴望某种食物」的成因无关。

questions.questionText: What do food companies do to capitalize on consumers' association with their food products?

options.label: A
options.text: They strive to influence how consumers remember their products.

options.label: B
options.text: They attempt to use consumers' long-term memories to promote addiction.

options.label: C
options.text: They try to exploit consumers' memories for their products as early as possible.

options.label: D
options.text: They endeavor to find what consumers remember about their products.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第四段指出「Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products」，shape the memories 即「影响、塑造消费者对产品的记忆」，与 A 的 influence how consumers remember 完全对应。故选 A。
questions.keySentence: Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products.

wrongOptions.B: 原文说的是塑造记忆，未提企业以长期记忆来「促成成瘾」这一因果链。
wrongOptions.C: 「尽早」是对 begin forming memories at a really early age 的误读，那是描述消费者形成记忆的时间，不是企业的做法。
wrongOptions.D: 企业是主动塑造记忆，而非被动地去「查明」消费者记住了什么。

questions.questionText: How does the food industry operate from manufacturing to packaging, according to Moss?

options.label: A
options.text: Placing the idea of fast food in an entirely new light.

options.label: B
options.text: Setting no limit to the number of fast food chains.

options.label: C
options.text: Focusing on how quickly the work is done.

options.label: D
options.text: Prioritizing the quality of their products.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第四段末句「Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging」与题干的 from manufacturing to packaging 完全对应，about speed 即「一切以快为要」，等同于 C 的 focusing on how quickly the work is done。故选 C。
questions.keySentence: Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging.

wrongOptions.A: 「让快餐概念呈现新含义」是莫斯本人的看法，不是行业的运作方式。
wrongOptions.B: 原文说的是「不限于快餐连锁店」，并非「不限制其数量」，属曲解。
wrongOptions.D: 行业优先的是速度、廉价与便利，文中并未提及以质量为先。

questions.questionText: Why are companies finding it difficult to satisfy consumers' demand for healthier food products?

options.label: A
options.text: They think speed of production outweighs consumers' health.

options.label: B
options.text: They believe their industry would perish without fast foods.

options.label: C
options.text: They have to strike a balance between taste and nutrition.

options.label: D
options.text: They are hooked on manufacturing convenience foods.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。末段指出企业难以满足健康饮食的新需求，原因是「because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods」，their own addiction 即 D 中的 are hooked on，呼应全文 hook 一词。故选 D。
questions.keySentence: these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods.

wrongOptions.A: 文中未做「速度重于消费者健康」的价值比较。
wrongOptions.B: 行业会否因缺少快餐而消亡，原文未涉及。
wrongOptions.C: 口味与营养的平衡是常识性推断，文中给出的原因是企业自身对方便食品生产的依赖。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Chimpanzees (黑猩猩), human beings' closest animal relatives, share up to 98% of our genes. Yet humans and chimpanzees lead very different lives. Fewer than 300,000 wild chimpanzees live in a few forested corners of Africa today, while humans have colonized every corner of the globe. At more than 7 billion, human population dwarfs that of nearly all other mammals — despite our physical weaknesses.
paragraphs.translation: 黑猩猩是人类最近的动物近亲，与我们共享高达 98% 的基因。然而人和黑猩猩过着截然不同的生活。如今野生黑猩猩不足 30 万只，栖息在非洲少数几片森林角落，而人类已遍布全球每一个角落。人口超过 70 亿，几乎让所有其他哺乳动物的数量都相形见绌——尽管我们在体能上处于弱势。

paragraphs.text: What could account for our species' incredible evolutionary successes?
paragraphs.translation: 是什么造就了我们这个物种惊人的进化成功？

paragraphs.text: One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe.
paragraphs.translation: 一个显而易见的答案是我们的大脑袋。也许正是我们与生俱来的智力，赋予了我们前所未有的跳出常规思考的能力，让人类在迁徙全球的过程中不断为棘手问题创造出解决办法。

paragraphs.text: But a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists (人类学家) are rejecting that explanation. They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.
paragraphs.translation: 但越来越多的认知科学家和人类学家否定了这一解释。他们认为，我们并非以创新者的身份谋生，恰恰是因为我们不自行思考才得以生存和繁盛。人们应对严酷气候与生态环境的方式，是小心翼翼地模仿他人。

paragraphs.text: In a famous study, psychologists Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten showed two groups of test subjects — children and chimpanzees — a mechanical box with a treat inside. In one condition, the box was opaque, while in the other it was transparent. The experimenters demonstrated how to open the box to retrieve the treat, but they also included the irrelevant step of tapping on the box with a stick.
paragraphs.translation: 在一项著名研究中，心理学家维多利亚·霍纳和安德鲁·怀滕向两组实验对象——儿童和黑猩猩——展示了一个里面装有零食的机械盒子。在一种条件下盒子不透明，另一种条件下则是透明的。实验者演示了如何打开盒子取出零食，但同时还加入了一个无关的步骤：用棍子敲盒子。

paragraphs.text: Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed.
paragraphs.translation: 奇怪的是，孩子们仔细地复制了打开盒子的所有步骤，哪怕他们能看出棍子毫无实际作用。也就是说，他们的模仿是非理性的：孩子们没有只做拿到奖励所必需的动作，而是亦步亦趋地模仿了看到的每一个动作。

paragraphs.text: Of course, that study only included three- and four-year-olds. But additional research has shown that older children and adults are even more likely to mindlessly copy others' actions, and infants are less likely to over-imitate — that is, to precisely copy even impractical actions.
paragraphs.translation: 当然，那项研究只涉及三四岁的儿童。但后续研究表明，年龄更大的儿童和成年人更可能不假思索地模仿他人的动作，而婴儿则较少出现过度模仿——即连不实用的动作也照搬不误。

paragraphs.text: By contrast, chimpanzees in the study only over-imitated in the opaque condition. In the transparent condition — where they saw that the stick was mechanically useless — they ignored that step entirely. Other research has since supported these findings.
paragraphs.translation: 相比之下，研究中的黑猩猩只在盒子不透明时才出现过度模仿。在透明条件下——它们看得出棍子在机械上毫无用处——就完全略过了那个步骤。此后的其他研究也支持了这些发现。

paragraphs.text: When it comes to copying, chimpanzees are more rational than human children or adults.
paragraphs.translation: 在模仿这件事上，黑猩猩比人类儿童或成人更理性。

paragraphs.text: Where does the seemingly irrational human preference for over-imitation come from? Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers.
paragraphs.translation: 人类这种看似非理性的过度模仿偏好从何而来？人类学家约瑟夫·亨里奇指出，世界各地的人们所依赖的技术往往复杂到没人能靠理性推演学会。人们只能一步一步地学，并信赖更有经验的长辈和同伴的智慧。

paragraphs.text: So the next time you hear someone arguing passionately that everyone should embrace nonconformity and avoid imitating others, you might laugh a little bit. We're not chimpanzees, after all.
paragraphs.translation: 所以下次当你听到有人慷慨激昂地主张人人都该特立独行、不要模仿他人时，你不妨会心一笑。毕竟，我们又不是黑猩猩。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What might explain humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals?

options.label: A
options.text: They are equipped with raw strength for solving the most challenging problems.

options.label: B
options.text: They cope with the outside world more effectively than their animal relatives.

options.label: C
options.text: They possess the most outstanding ability to think.

options.label: D
options.text: They know how to survive everywhere on earth.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第一段末提出人口数量让其他哺乳动物相形见绌，第二段设问其进化成功的原因，第三段给出「One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box」，即最直观的解释是人类超群的思考能力。故选 C。
questions.keySentence: One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box.

wrongOptions.A: 原文是 raw intelligence（天生智力）而非 raw strength（体力），且第一段明说人类 physical weaknesses。
wrongOptions.B: 「比动物近亲更有效地应对外部世界」是笼统概括，未落到 big brains 这一具体解释上。
wrongOptions.D: 遍布全球是结果的描述，而非题干所问的原因。

questions.questionText: What accounts for humans' evolutionary successes according to a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists?

options.label: A
options.text: They are better at innovating solutions.

options.label: B
options.text: They thrive through creative strategies.

options.label: C
options.text: They are naturally adaptive to ecological contexts.

options.label: D
options.text: They meet challenges by imitating others carefully.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第四段说这批学者否定「大脑聪明」的解释，认为「we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others」，carefully copying others 即 D 的 imitating others carefully。故选 D。
questions.keySentence: Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.

wrongOptions.A: 原文明确写道 rather than making our living as innovators，即否定创新说，属反向干扰。
wrongOptions.B: 创造性策略同属被否定的「靠自己思考」一派观点。
wrongOptions.C: 人类应对生态环境靠的是模仿他人，而非「天生具有适应性」。

questions.questionText: What does the author think is odd about the findings of the study by Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten?

options.label: A
options.text: Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters.

options.label: B
options.text: Chimpanzees could tell the transparent box from the opaque one.

options.label: C
options.text: Chimpanzees could retrieve the treat more quickly than children did.

options.label: D
options.text: Children omitted the step of tapping on the box with a stick to open it.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。题干中的 odd 直接对应原文段首的 Oddly：「Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps... they copied irrationally: ... children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed」，即孩子非理性地照搬了实验者的每个动作。故选 A。
questions.keySentence: Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect.

wrongOptions.B: 黑猩猩区分透明与不透明盒子是文中作为对照给出的理性表现，作者并未称之为奇怪。
wrongOptions.C: 取到零食的速度快慢，文中从未比较。
wrongOptions.D: 略过敲盒子这一步的是黑猩猩（透明条件下），孩子恰恰照做了，与原文相反。

questions.questionText: What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying?

options.label: A
options.text: It originates in the rationality of people around the world.

options.label: B
options.text: It stems from the way people learn complex technologies.

options.label: C
options.text: It results from people distrusting their own wisdom.

options.label: D
options.text: It derives from the desire to acquire knowledge step by step.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。倒数第二段亨里奇指出人们依赖的技术复杂到无法靠理性学会，「Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers」，即模仿偏好源自人们学习复杂技术的方式。故选 B。
questions.keySentence: people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step.

wrongOptions.A: 原文恰恰说这些技术 no one can learn them rationally，与「源于人的理性」相反。
wrongOptions.C: 人们信赖的是更有经验者的智慧，文中未说他们「不信任自己的智慧」。
wrongOptions.D: step by step 是学习复杂技术时不得已的方式，不是「渴望逐步获取知识」这一主观愿望。

questions.questionText: What point does the author want to emphasize when he says "We're not chimpanzees"?

options.label: A
options.text: It is arguable whether everyone should avoid imitation.

options.label: B
options.text: It is characteristic of human beings to copy others.

options.label: C
options.text: It is desirable to trust in more knowledgeable peers.

options.label: D
options.text: It is naive to laugh at someone embracing nonconformity.

questions.analysis: 推理判断题。全文对比表明：在模仿上黑猩猩更理性，而人类会过度模仿。末段说听到有人主张「人人都该特立独行、别模仿别人」时不妨一笑，理由是「We're not chimpanzees」——不模仿是黑猩猩的做派，模仿他人才是人类的本性。故选 B。
questions.keySentence: So the next time you hear someone arguing passionately that everyone should embrace nonconformity and avoid imitating others, you might laugh a little bit. We're not chimpanzees, after all.

wrongOptions.A: 作者的态度是明确的（模仿是人类天性），并非认为此事「有争议」。
wrongOptions.C: 信赖更有见识的同伴是亨里奇解释中的一环，不是这句反讽所强调的要点。
wrongOptions.D: 作者本人正是那个 laugh a little bit 的人，说嘲笑特立独行者「幼稚」与原文立场相反。

questionGroups.sourceText: 近年来，越来越多的中国文化产品走向全球市场，日益受到海外消费者的青睐。随着中国对外文化贸易的快速发展，中国文化产品出口额已持续多年位居世界前列，形成了一批具有国际影响力的文化企业、产品和品牌。数据显示，中国的出版物、影视作品、网络文学与动漫作品等在海外的销售量连年攀升。中国政府出台了一系列政策鼓励和支持更多具有中国元素的优秀文化产品走出国门，扩大海外市场份额，进一步提升中国文化的世界影响力。

answer.modelTranslation: In recent years, an increasing number of Chinese cultural products have entered the global market and won growing popularity among overseas consumers. With the rapid growth of China's foreign cultural trade, the export value of Chinese cultural products has ranked among the highest in the world for many consecutive years, giving rise to a group of cultural enterprises, products and brands with international influence. Statistics show that overseas sales of Chinese publications, films and television works, online literature and animation works have been rising year after year. The Chinese government has introduced a series of policies to encourage and support more outstanding cultural products featuring Chinese elements in going global, expanding their share of overseas markets and further enhancing the worldwide influence of Chinese culture.
translationNotes: 「近年来」用 In recent years 引导，主句用现在完成时 have entered，体现持续到现在的变化。
「走向全球市场」译作 enter the global market 或 go global 均可，避免直译为 walk to。
「日益受到……青睐」用 win growing popularity among... 表达，比 be liked by 更书面。
「随着……的快速发展」用 With the rapid growth of... 介词短语作状语，避免再起一个从句。
「对外文化贸易」译为 foreign cultural trade；「出口额」为 export value，不用 export amount of money。
「持续多年位居世界前列」用 has ranked among the highest in the world for many consecutive years，consecutive 对应「持续多年」。
「形成了一批……」用现在分词短语 giving rise to a group of... 承接前句，避免句子零散。
「数据显示」用 Statistics show that 引导宾语从句；「连年攀升」用 have been rising year after year，现在完成进行时体现持续上升。
「出台了一系列政策」固定表达 has introduced/rolled out a series of policies。
「具有中国元素的」用现在分词 featuring Chinese elements 后置修饰，比定语从句更简洁；「走出国门」译作 go global，与首句呼应但不重复用词。
scoringPoints: 首句时态：用现在完成时或一般现在时体现「近年来……越来越多」的持续趋势。
「日益受到海外消费者的青睐」需译出被动或 win popularity 结构，不可漏译 overseas consumers。
「出口额已持续多年位居世界前列」需译出「出口额」这一主语与「多年」这一时间跨度。
「形成了一批具有国际影响力的文化企业、产品和品牌」三个并列名词需完整译出，并保留 international influence。
第三句四类文化产品（出版物、影视作品、网络文学、动漫作品）为得分点，需逐项对应。
末句三个并列目的（走出国门、扩大海外市场份额、提升世界影响力）建议用并列动名词或不定式统一处理，保持结构一致。
